supporting: Trusted Types and CSP as additional controls

claims.claim: XSS prevention requires a combination of defensive techniques rather than a single technique.
Output encoding must match the HTML, attribute, URL, CSS, or JavaScript context because browsers parse these contexts differently.

When user-provided content should be plain text, `textContent` avoids parsing it as HTML; MDN advises against `innerHTML` for setting text because it deals with raw HTML and can be susceptible to XSS.
When an application intentionally permits user-authored HTML, HTML sanitization is a distinct requirement, and modifying sanitized content later can undermine the protection.
Modern framework template protections can reduce XSS bugs, but developers must understand gaps created by escape hatches and other insecure uses.
`innerHTML` parses its input as HTML and is an injection sink when a supplied string originated from an attacker.
